briefs.headline: West Virginia women fall to No. 13 Notre Dame 78-64 at the Battle 4 Atlantis
briefs.summary: Notre Dame defeated No. 22 West Virginia 78-64 at Imperial Arena on Paradise Island, Bahamas, on Thursday before 326, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Hannah Hidalgo scored 22 points with nine steals to become Notre Dame's career scoring leader, and Jacy Abii had 16 points and 12 rebounds as the Irish led 23-11 after a quarter, 43-26 at halftime and by as many as 21 while outrebounding the Mountaineers 48-33, 21-11 on the offensive glass. Gia Cooke had 18 points and Zahirah Walton 17 with eight steals for West Virginia, which shot 4 of 21 from 3-point range and committed 24 turnovers against 21 for Notre Dame; the Mountaineers outscored the Irish 25-20 in the fourth quarter. West Virginia, which had beaten Florida 70-62 on Tuesday, is 6-1; ESPN's schedule lists no further Atlantis game and the next game as Coppin State at Hope Coliseum on Monday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Bengals hold Risner and Allen out of a second straight practice before the Saints
briefs.summary: Right guard Dalton Risner (knees) and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (rest) did not participate in the Bengals' Thursday practice for a second day, and defensive tackle B.J. Hill was limited for rest after practicing fully Wednesday, per the club's Week 12 injury report updated Thursday afternoon; safety Bryan Cook (ankle), cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) and receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) were full participants again, with Davis and Iosivas designated for return from reserve lists. New Orleans held tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring and wrist) out again, upgraded center Erik McCoy (biceps) to full and limited tackles Taliese Fuaga and Asim Richards, guard David Edwards and linebacker Peter Werner. Game statuses come with Friday's report. The Bengals, first in the AFC North, host the Saints on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

briefs.headline: JSA says seven sekitori will miss the winter tour as Hatsu basho sits 44 days out
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association said Thursday that seven sekitori (salaried wrestlers in the top two divisions) will miss the winter jungyo (regional tour), which opens Sunday in Amakusa, Kumamoto Prefecture, and runs through Dec. 20 in Uruma, Okinawa, Nikkan Sports reported: six makuuchi (top-division) men including Takayasu, Kotoeiho, Shishi and Ichiyamamoto, and one from juryo (second division). No one ranked sanyaku (the three ranks below yokozuna) or higher is out, and yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, nine wins and six losses in Fukuoka, joins from the first day; six juryo men including Kagayaki and Shodai fill the places. The JSA's schedule page lists the banzuke (rankings) for the Hatsu basho (New Year tournament) for release Dec. 21, with the tournament opening Jan. 10 at the Kokugikan in Tokyo, 44 days out, and closing Jan. 24.

briefs.headline: Bears beat Lions 39-35 on Williams' touchdown pass with 3 seconds left
briefs.summary: Chicago defeated Detroit 39-35 at Ford Field on Thanksgiving before 64,316 to take sole possession of first place in the NFC North, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Caleb Williams completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns, the last a 6-yard throw to Rome Odunze in the back corner of the end zone for the Bears' first lead of the game, after Detroit had led by 11 midway through the fourth quarter on Jahmyr Gibbs' 70-yard run, his third score. Chicago (9-2) has won six straight; Detroit is 8-3. Williams had his midsection examined after the game and said scans showed nothing.

briefs.headline: Eagles beat Cowboys 39-38 on Elliott's 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds left
briefs.summary: Philadelphia defeated Dallas 39-38 at AT&T Stadium before 93,417, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, after Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer went for it on fourth-and-1 at the Philadelphia 39 with a two-point lead and 55 seconds left and Dak Prescott was sacked; Jake Elliott's 59-yard kick followed. Joe Milton started at quarterback for the Eagles (4-7); the Cowboys fell to 5-7. Schottenheimer said he did not second-guess the call. In the night game, Buffalo beat Kansas City 13-10 in rain and wind at Highmark Stadium on Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal as time expired; Josh Allen was 10 of 21 for 81 yards with two interceptions, James Cook ran for 117 yards and the Bills are 10-1 atop the AFC, with the Chiefs 8-3. Pittsburgh hosts Denver today at 3 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: No. 25 Louisville beats No. 13 St. John's 93-90 on Wooley's buzzer-beater to reach the Players Era final
briefs.summary: Louisville defeated St. John's 93-90 in a Players Era semifinal in Las Vegas on Thursday night when Adrian Wooley hit a 3-pointer at the buzzer from Seth Trimble's pass, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. The Cardinals are five and one and the Red Storm six and one.

briefs.headline: Saint Mary's hands No. 6 UCLA its first loss in San Diego
briefs.summary: Saint Mary's made 15 3-pointers and defeated No. 6 UCLA 85 to 70 in the Rady Children's Invitational on Thursday, with Jeremy Dent-Smith scoring 21, per ESPN. In the Players Era consolation round in Las Vegas, No. 5 Texas Tech came from behind against Oregon, 62 to 59, and No. 22 Gonzaga finished 72 to 64 over Baylor. There were no NBA games Thursday.

The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

Geese, ducks, doves, woodcock and snipe are not in the table, which points to WVDNR's separate migratory bird regulations and says HIP registration is required, so no migratory date is printed. The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

prime.limit: 14- to 20-inch total length slot, one fish greater than 26 inches allowed; 3 per day
prime.item: Prime by the reference file's November calendar, and the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report of Nov. 1, 26 days old this morning, has the sound's bite moving to trout as the water cools; the water at Beaufort read 60.6F at 5:30 a.m. The NCDMF table reads spotted seatrout at a 14- to 20-inch total length slot with one fish greater than 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulations. The current trout proclamation on NCDMF's index is FF-31-2026, issued June 25, 2026, and effective July 1, 2026, opening and harvest restrictions, and no newer trout proclamation appears; the newest entry on the index is FF-52-2026 of Nov. 23 on commercial spiny dogfish, and nothing was issued Nov. 24 to 27. Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requires recreational trout harvest to be reported to the division. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning, Friday, Nov. 27; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force or effect, and that fishery rules are subject to change.

prime.limit: 18-inch minimum, 27-inch maximum total length; 1 per day
prime.item: Prime by the reference file's November calendar; the Nov. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 26 days old, has the piers taking red drum of 32 inches and more on the north end of the island and smaller reds in the sound and surf. The NCDMF table reads red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day, under note (C), which reads that it is unlawful to possess red drum greater than 27 inches total length; recreational red drum harvest must be reported to the division under commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124, which proclamation FF-27-2026 also recites. No red drum proclamation appears on the index for 2026. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning, Friday, Nov. 27; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force or effect, and that fishery rules are subject to change.

prime.species: Sheepshead, bluefish, Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and black drum
prime.limit: Sheepshead 14-inch total length, 5 per day; bluefish no minimum, 5 per day; Spanish mackerel 12-inch fork length, 15 per day; king mackerel 24-inch fork length, 3 per day; black drum 14- to 25-inch slot, 10 per day, one over 25 inches allowed
prime.item: The NCDMF table reads sheepshead at 14-inch total length, five per day, with FF-16-2026 of March 13, 2026, effective March 16, as the sheepshead proclamation on the index; bluefish at no minimum and five per day, note (M) reading that the recreational creel is five fish per person per day in all private, non-for-hire fisheries; Spanish mackerel at 12-inch fork length, 15 per day, and king mackerel at 24-inch fork length, three per day, both under note (H), which defers to the most recent mackerel proclamation. Black drum reads a 14- to 25-inch total length slot and 10 per day, with note (C) allowing one black drum over 25 inches per person per day. The Nov. 1 Fisherman's Post report has Surf City Pier on black drum, pompano and croaker on the bottom and Jolly Roger Pier with bluefish thick in the early mornings, a month-old pattern and not this morning's conditions. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning, Friday, Nov. 27; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force or effect, and that fishery rules are subject to change.

prime.species: Black sea bass (south of Cape Hatteras)
prime.limit: 13-inch total length, measured without the tail filament; 7 per day
prime.item: Open on Topsail's side of the cape with no closed period in the proclamation: FF-45-2026, issued Oct. 20, 2026, by the division's interim director and effective Oct. 28, 2026, superseding FF-40-2026 and implementing Regulatory Amendment 36 to the South Atlantic snapper grouper plan, reads for black sea bass south of Cape Hatteras that it is unlawful to possess fish less than 13 inches total length, tip of the snout to the tip of the tail excluding the filament, or more than seven per person per day. The same proclamation closes gag, black grouper, scamp and the other shallow-water groupers outside May 1 through Dec. 31, closed gag after Aug. 1, 2026, for the year, and reads red snapper, snowy grouper and golden tilefish as unlawful to possess, the latter two reopening May 1 and Jan. 1, 2027. North of Cape Hatteras the table reads black sea bass at 13 inches, 15 per day, season open May 1 to Dec. 31, 34 days off. The Nov. 1 Fisherman's Post report has Plan 9 Charters on black sea bass with snapper and triggerfish in 60 to 80 feet and more on cut bait and jigs. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, effective Nov. 1, 2026, and proclamation FF-45-2026, both read this morning.

going_out.limit: Flounder, all species: unlawful to possess outside Sept. 1 to 14, 2026. Striped bass, Central Southern Management Area: unlawful to possess
going_out.item: Not closing, closed: proclamation FF-27-2026, issued June 3, 2026, at 11:30 a.m. by the division's director and superseding FF-17-2026, reads that it shall be unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. on Sept. 1, 2026, until 11:59 p.m. on Sept. 14, 2026, in internal coastal and joint fishing waters and Atlantic Ocean waters, with a 15-inch minimum and one fish per person per day inside that window, and the NCDMF table lists flounder of all species as unlawful to possess. The flounder proclamations issued since, FF-44 of Oct. 15, FF-47 of Oct. 23, FF-48 of Oct. 27 and FF-51 of Nov. 20, are all commercial. The table's striped bass line reads unlawful to possess with note (A) reading that in the Central Southern Management Area, where Topsail sits, it is unlawful to possess striped bass including hybrid bass, that the Albemarle Sound season is closed and that the Atlantic Ocean carries one per person per day in a 28- to 31-inch total length slot year-round; tarpon are unlawful to possess. The index's newest entry is FF-52-2026 of Nov. 23, effective Nov. 25, on commercial spiny dogfish, and nothing was issued Nov. 24 to 27. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, effective Nov. 1, 2026, the proclamations index and FF-27-2026, all read this morning, Friday, Nov. 27.

waters.reading: 644 cfs, 3.2 feet at 5:15 a.m., rising on both flow and stage against 74.4 cfs and 1.48 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.read: 644 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 644 cfs and 3.2 feet at 5:15 a.m., against 74.4 cfs and 1.48 feet 24 hours earlier, and both trends read rising: the river has come up nearly ninefold on flow and 1.72 feet on stage overnight, from the 71 cfs the fetcher called prime wading water on Thanksgiving morning. The fetcher's verdict is the paper's: 644 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank. At this flow and still rising the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the config records are one brown current, the seams are gone, and there is no wading setup for the Williams today; what the weekend holds depends on the gauge turning over and falling, which this desk does not forecast. From the bank, the one pattern the water's own structure supports is a large dark sculpin streamer on a sink tip, swung into the slack of the inside bends and the eddies below the plunge pools where fish pushed off their lies by the surge hold out of the current, with sculpin the forage that a rising, coloured river puts on the move; it is a bank cast, not a wade. The gauge, not the calendar, decides when the long-leader small-fly water comes back.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.15 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.76 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.1 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: This is the upstream bracket, the pool side, 14 miles above the dam. Normal pool and ordinary bank access, up 0.39 of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading rising after two mornings flat at 24.8, the pool taking the same water that has the Williams and the other Allegheny tributaries up. A rising pool at normal stage still fishes structure, with one change: the current picks up along the faces of the wing dams and the riprap and the fish slide to the downstream side of them, so the pattern is the slack water and the eddy behind each wing dam rather than the face, a white or shad-pattern swimbait on a half-ounce head swum along the seam where the current breaks off the end of the dam, shad being the forage the config records, and a jig with a crawfish trailer, the other forage on the list, dragged down the riprap on the slack side where the bank current eases. The water will carry more colour as it comes up, so the swimbait goes to a darker shad pattern or chartreuse and the retrieve slows. The barge cuts hold the fish that have left the current altogether. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.68 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 26.17 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.7 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: This is the downstream bracket, below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch. Normal pool with ordinary bank access, up 0.51 of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading rising, so both gauges that bracket the dam are climbing and the river is moving through the reach for the first time this week. More water through the gates means more current below them, and the pattern tightens to the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad, the forage the config records, stack in the churn and the fish hold on the edges of it, so a one-ounce spoon or a heavy jig worked along the current seams off the lock wall, or a live skipjack drifted down the same seams, is the hybrid striper and catfish setup, with the rising water pushing the holding fish toward the slack side of the wall and the eddies at the ends of the wing dams. Sauger and walleye hold on the bottom at the tail of the seams in late November and take a jig and minnow or a blade bait fished vertically along the lock wall and in the barge cuts, and a rising, colouring river moves them shallower on the riprap, where a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side of the bank current covers them.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 3:57 AM at -0.3 ft, high 10:11 AM at 4.5 ft, low 4:59 PM at 0.1 ft, high 10:31 PM at 3.2 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:20 AM at -0.5 ft, high 9:03 AM at 6.0 ft, low 3:33 PM at -0.2 ft, high 9:25 PM at 4.1 ft. Water 60.6F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waning gibbous, 92% illuminated, 17.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 10:11 AM and 10:31 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The moon is a waning gibbous at 92% and 17.5 days old, three days past full and four or five days short of the last quarter, so the spring tides are easing toward neap and the table shows the swings narrowing: the sound at Hampstead rises 4.8 feet from the 3:57 AM low at -0.3 to the 10:11 AM high at 4.5, the afternoon ebb drops 4.4 feet to the 4:59 PM low at 0.1, and the evening flood climbs 3.1 feet to the 10:31 PM high at 3.2; all four events fall inside Friday and none spills over. Neap approaching means gentler current through the inlet and less bait moved on each change than the week of the full moon, so the moving-water windows are softer and the first and last hour of each change matter more. The surf station at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead of the sound, 97 minutes on the morning low, 68 on the morning high, 86 on the afternoon low and 66 on the evening high, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, so the ebb at the crew's spot runs six hours and 48 minutes, from 10:11 to 4:59. The water at Beaufort read 60.6F at 5:30 a.m., down 1.1 degrees on Thursday's 61.7F. Beach conditions: NWS Newport/Morehead City, in an advisory issued at 4:21 a.m. Friday, has a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Onslow, which includes North Topsail Beach, the lower New River and the adjacent tidal creeks, until 10 a.m. EST Friday, for 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, with dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion; NWS Wilmington has nothing active for Coastal Pender this morning. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 26 days old, with no December report posted as of this morning, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking red drum of 32 inches and more on the north end, smaller reds and the occasional trout in the sound and surf; Native Son has trout turning on in the creeks on the 5-to-8-foot seams as the weather settles and cut bait the best producer for the reds inside; Speckled Specialist reports smaller trout plentiful with some to 28 inches, live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 8 feet and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials; Carolina Flats has topwater early to locate trout, deeper holes later and soft plastics for reds on the oyster and grass banks; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to Friday's table and water at 60.6F: the morning flood into the 10:11 high is the first window, and with the Onslow advisory running to 10 a.m. the sound side of the island, not the beach, is where it fishes, trout on the last hour of the flood along the grass edges and the ICWW channel edge with a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly on the bottom in 60-degree water, or a live shrimp under a popping cork over the oyster bars. Red drum's window, the last of the fall, runs roughly 2:30 p.m. to the 4:59 low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet, the forage the config records, on a half-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges where the draining grass dumps shrimp and mud minnows, or a soft plastic over the oyster bars as the water leaves them, with the softer neap-side ebb keeping the bait in the channels longer. Trout again on the first of the evening flood after the 4:59 low through last light in the 4-to-8-foot creek seams; the hour before the 10:31 PM high falls after dark, and the dock lights on that flood are the night trout water. Spot and sea mullet take bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood, 8 to 10:31 p.m. Flounder are release only under FF-27-2026.
